title: The Radiators of the reservoir
premise: Dominic Vasquez, a restaurant critic whose palate has gone numb along with his sense of belonging, returns to the reservoir town of his childhood for his estranged father's funeral. There, a stranger greets the family by 'the Radiators'—a name from a life his father led that no one at home ever spoke of. As Dominic traces this hidden identity through old friends, letters, and a woman named Marisol who loved his father first, he uncovers a decades-old choice between duty and love that mirrors his own hollow marriage and stalled career. In the end, Dominic must decide whether to protect the family myth or tell the truth aloud; he chooses truth, delivering a eulogy under the real name at the water's edge, and in speaking it finally tastes something again.
about_author: August Halloran is a former line cook turned essayist who writes about food, memory, and the families we inherit twice. They live near a reservoir and still set an extra plate at dinner, just in case.

chapters.title: The Tenant
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. A numb restaurant critic files a glowing review of a meal he couldn't taste, then learns his father has died. He drives back to the reservoir town he fled twenty years ago, feeling like a guest in his own life. Emotional beat: disconnection sharpening into dread.

chapters.title: A Name Nobody Uses
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. At the wake, a weathered stranger embraces Dominic's mother and calls the family 'the Radiators.' She goes pale; the stranger leaves before questions form. Dominic finds the word scrawled inside his father's old tackle box. Emotional beat: the first crack in the official story.

chapters.title: What the Water Keeps
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. He walks the reservoir shore where his father once fished, interviewing a bait-shop owner who slips and mentions 'Ray'—not his father's name, Rafael. The shopkeeper clams up, frightened of someone. Emotional beat: curiosity curdling into suspicion.

chapters.title: Marisol
chapters.summary: POV alternating Dominic and Marisol. Dominic tracks down Marisol Reyes, who feeds him a home-cooked meal he can almost taste. She recognizes him instantly as Rafael's son but refuses to explain, saying some goodbyes take forty years. Emotional beat: warmth threatening the numbness.

chapters.title: The Second Family
chapters.summary: POV Marisol. Flashback to 1979: Rafael, a young laborer building the dam, falls for Marisol while promised to another. When the reservoir flooded the valley, he chose duty—the other woman, the respectable name—and let 'Rafael' drown with the town. Emotional beat: love sacrificed on the altar of obligation.

chapters.title: Letters Under the Floorboard
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. Searching his parents' house, Dominic finds forty years of unmailed letters addressed to Marisol, signed Rafael. His mother catches him; she has always known, and her silence was her own act of loyalty. Emotional beat: betrayal revealed as a shared wound, not a simple lie.

chapters.title: The Man Who Objects
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. The stranger from the wake reappears—it's Marisol's brother, who believes Rafael stole Marisol's life and wants the truth buried with him. He threatens to expose everything at the funeral unless the family keeps quiet. Emotional beat: rising pressure; truth now has a price and a deadline.

chapters.title: Tasting Again
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. On the eve of the funeral, Marisol cooks Rafael's favorite dish one last time. Dominic eats it and weeps—he can taste it. He realizes his palate died when he stopped speaking honestly, and that his own marriage is repeating his father's silence. Emotional beat: restoration through confession.

chapters.title: The Eulogy
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. At the graveside, with his mother's nod and the brother watching, Dominic abandons the safe speech and tells the whole story aloud: Rafael, Marisol, the name, the choice. The mourners hold their breath; his mother takes his hand. Emotional beat: climax—truth spoken at last, out loud, whatever it costs.

chapters.title: The Reservoir Gives Back
chapters.summary: POV Dominic, coda with Marisol. Weeks later, Dominic leaves his marriage honestly rather than silently, writes his first true review, and shares a final meal with Marisol at the water's edge. The reservoir glitters over the drowned town, holding nothing back anymore. Emotional beat: resolution—belonging earned by telling the truth.
